• The **Constitution of India** was adopted by the **Constituent Assembly** on **26th November 1949** and officially came into force on **26th January 1950**.
 
• At the time of its original enactment, the Constitution contained a **Preamble**, **395 Articles** categorized into **22 Parts**, and exactly **8 Schedules**.

questions.question: Which language was added to the Eighth Schedule by the 92nd Amendment (2003)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**All of the above**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **92nd Constitutional Amendment Act** was enacted in **2003** to include four additional languages in the **Eighth Schedule** of the Constitution of India.
 
• The four languages added through this amendment were **Bodo**, **Dogri**, **Maithili**, and **Santhali**.
 
• **Bodo** is a language primarily spoken in the **Bodoland Territorial Region** of **Assam** and belongs to the Tibeto-Burman language family.
 
• **Maithili** is an Indo-Aryan language spoken predominantly in the **Mithila region** of **Bihar** and parts of **Jharkhand**.
 
• **Santhali** is the most widely spoken Munda language, used by the **Santhal tribal community** residing in **Jharkhand**, **Odisha**, **West Bengal**, and **Bihar**.
 
• Following the inclusion of these four languages, the total count of recognized languages in the **Eighth Schedule** increased from **18** to **22**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Eighth Schedule** originally consisted of **14** languages at the time of the Constitution's commencement.

 
 
• The **21st Amendment Act, 1967** introduced **Sindhi** as the 15th language.
 
• The **71st Amendment Act, 1992** added three more languages: **Konkani**, **Manipuri**, and **Nepali**.
 
• **Dogri**, the fourth language added in 2003 along with Bodo, Maithili, and Santhali, is spoken primarily in the **Jammu and Kashmir** region.
 
 
 
• Constitutional provisions related to official languages are found in **Part XVII**, covering **Articles 343 to 351**.
 
 
• **Article 344(1)** provides for the constitution of a Commission by the **President of India** to make recommendations regarding the progressive use of Hindi for official purposes.
 
• **Article 351** provides a directive for the development and promotion of the **Hindi language** as a medium of expression for the composite culture of India.

questions.question: During which occasions is Giddha commonly performed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Weddings and harvest festivals**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Giddha** is a popular and vibrant folk dance originating from the **Punjab** region of India and Pakistan, specifically performed by **women**.
 
• The dance is a hallmark of joyous occasions and is most commonly performed during the **harvest season**, particularly during the festival of **Baisakhi**, which marks the Punjabi New Year and the reaping of **Rabi crops**.
 
• It is an essential part of **Punjabi weddings**, where female relatives and friends gather to celebrate the union through rhythmic movements and playful singing.
 
• The performance is characterized by the singing of **Boliyan** (short traditional couplets) that express a wide range of emotions, from humor and teasing to domestic life and social commentary.
 
• Unlike formal classical dances, **Giddha** is a social activity that takes place during **Teeyan** (the monsoon festival) and other family celebrations like the birth of a child.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Performance Characteristics**:

 
 
• **Style and Form**: It is often considered the feminine counterpart to **Bhangra**. While Bhangra is high-intensity and athletic, Giddha focuses on grace, elegance, and rhythmic **clapping** (Taali).
 
• **Musical Accompaniment**: The primary rhythm is created by the dancers’ hands, but it is often supported by a **Dholak** (a two-headed hand drum) played by an elder woman or a professional musician.
 
• **Attire**: Dancers wear bright-colored **Salwar Kameez** or **Lehengas** paired with heavily embroidered **Phulkari** dupattas. Key traditional ornaments include the **Sagghi Phul** (hair ornament) and heavy necklaces.
 
• **Cultural Significance**: It serves as a medium for women to express their creative energy and share their lived experiences in a patriarchal society through the medium of **storytelling** and dance.

questions.question: Who determined the value of the universal gravitational constant G?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Henry Cavendish**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Universal Gravitational Constant**, represented by the symbol **G**, is a fundamental physical constant that appears in **Sir Isaac Newton's law of universal gravitation**.
 
• **Henry Cavendish**, an English physicist and chemist, successfully determined the value of **G** through a series of experiments conducted between **1797 and 1798**, known as the **Cavendish experiment**.
 
• The primary objective of his experiment was to measure the **density of the Earth**, but the results provided the first accurate calculation of the gravitational constant.
 
• Cavendish utilized a **torsion balance**, which featured a horizontal wooden rod suspended by a thin wire with small **lead spheres** at each end; he measured the tiny gravitational attraction between these and larger stationary lead masses.
 
• By observing the **deflection** of the rod and the **twisting** of the suspension wire, he quantified the force of gravity, leading to the derivation of **G**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Isaac Newton**:

 
 
• Formulated the **Inverse Square Law** of gravitation in his work **Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica** in **1687**.
 
• While he identified the relationship **F = G × m₁m₂ / r²**, he did not possess the experimental means to measure the value of **G**.
 
 
 
• **Johannes Kepler**:
 
 
• Famous for his **three laws of planetary motion** which described the orbits of planets as ellipses.
 
• His work was purely **kinematic** and did not include the gravitational constant or the physical cause of planetary motion.
 
 
 
• **Albert Einstein**:
 
 
• Proposed the **General Theory of Relativity** in **1915**, redefining gravity as the **curvature of spacetime** rather than a standard force.
 
 
 
• The value of **G** is approximately **6.674 × 10−¹¹ N m² kg−²**.

questions.question: What is the official match duration in senior-level men's kabaddi under Asian Kabaddi Federation rules?

options.text: 40 minutes (two halves of 20 minutes) with a 5-minute break

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**40 min (two halves of 20 min) with a 5-min break**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the official rules set by the **Asian Kabaddi Federation (AKF)** and the **International Kabaddi Federation (IKF)**, a standard senior-level men's kabaddi match consists of **40 minutes** of active play.
 
• This duration is divided into two equal halves of **20 minutes** each, ensuring a balanced competition for both teams.
 
• A mandatory **5-minute interval** is provided between the first and second halves, allowing players to recover and strategize while teams switch sides of the **kabaddi court**.
 
• The match clock is strictly managed by the **official timekeeper** and may be paused during specific events such as injury treatments or official reviews, but the standard playing time remains fixed at **40 minutes**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Match Categories and Variations:**

 
 
• For **Senior Women** and **Junior Boys/Girls**, the duration is typically reduced to **30 minutes**, split into two halves of **15 minutes** each, with a **5-minute break**.
 
• In professional leagues like the **Pro Kabaddi League (PKL)**, the 40-minute format is maintained to align with international standards.
 
 
 
• **Time-Outs and Substitutions:**
 
 
• Each team is permitted **two time-outs** of **30 seconds** each per half.
 
• Teams are allowed a maximum of **five substitutions** during the match to manage player fatigue or tactical changes.
 
 
 
• **Tie-Breaker Rules:**
 
 
• If a knockout match ends in a draw, **extra time** is played, usually consisting of two halves of **5 minutes** each.
 
• If the score remains tied after extra time, the match is decided by a **Golden Raid** or a series of five raids by each team.

questions.question: In tennis, what does a score of "deuce" mean?

options.text: The game is tied, but not at 40-40.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The score is tied at 40-40.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the sport of **Tennis**, the term **Deuce** describes a specific situation in a game where both the server and the receiver have won three points each, resulting in a score of **40-40**.
 
• The traditional scoring progression in a tennis game follows the sequence of **Love** (0 points), **15** (1 point), **30** (2 points), and **40** (3 points). When both sides reach 40, the score is called **Deuce** rather than 40-all.
 
• Once a game reaches deuce, a player must win **two consecutive points** to win the game. The first point won after deuce gives that player the **Advantage**, and the second consecutive point secures the game.
 
• If the player with the advantage loses the next point, the score returns to **Deuce**. This cycle continues until one player wins two points in a row from a deuce state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Scoring Terminology**:

 
 
• **Love**: Refers to a score of **zero**. It is widely believed to have originated from the **French** word **l'oeuf** (meaning egg), which symbolizes the shape of a zero.
 
• **Advantage In (Ad-in)**: This is the score when the **Server** wins the first point after a deuce.
 
• **Advantage Out (Ad-out)**: This occurs when the **Receiver** wins the first point following a deuce.
 
 
 
• **Etymology and Rules**:
 
 
• The word **Deuce** is derived from the **French** word **deux**, meaning two, or the phrase **à deux de jeu**, signifying that the players are two points away from winning the game.
 
• In some modern formats, such as **Professional Doubles** or certain amateur leagues, **No-Ad (No Advantage)** scoring is used. In this system, a **deciding point** is played at deuce, and the winner of that single point wins the entire game immediately.

questions.question: What is the key condition for earning a bonus point in kabaddi?

options.text: Crossing the bonus line with one foot while another is in the air

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Crossing the bonus line with one foot while another is in the air**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bonus Line** is a specific marking located in the opponent's territory, exactly 1 meter beyond the **Baulk Line** toward the end line.
 
• A raider earns a **bonus point** by crossing this line with one foot while the other foot remains **completely in the air**, ensuring no part of the trailing foot is touching the ground behind the line.
 
• This rule is only applicable when the defending team has at least **6 or 7 players** active on the mat; if the number of defenders drops to 5 or fewer, the bonus point rule becomes **inactive**.
 
• The point is awarded immediately upon the successful completion of the action, even if the raider is subsequently **tackled** or caught during the same raid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Baulk Line**:

 
 
• Every raider must cross this line at least once during a raid to make the raid **legal**; failing to do so results in the raider being declared **out**.
 
 
 
• **Point System and Revivals**:
 
 
• A **Bonus Point** adds 1 point to the team total but, unlike a **Touch Point**, it does not allow for the **revival** of a teammate from the sitting block.
 
• A **Touch Point** is scored when the raider tags one or more defenders and returns safely to their own half of the court.
 
 
 
• **Lona**:
 
 
• An additional **2 points** are awarded as a **Lona** when a team manages to put the entire opposing team out, necessitating a full-team reset on the mat.

questions.question: The Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC) was established for:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Multipurpose river valley development**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC)** was established on **July 7, 1948**, as the first **multipurpose river valley project** of independent India.
 
• It was created through an Act of the **Constituent Assembly of India** to manage the **Damodar River** basin, which was historically known as the **Sorrow of Bengal** due to devastating floods.
 
• The project was modeled after the **Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA)** of the **United States**, focusing on the unified development of a river basin spanning **West Bengal** and **Jharkhand** (formerly part of Bihar).
 
• The primary objectives of the corporation include **flood control**, **irrigation**, **water supply** for domestic and industrial use, and **soil conservation**.
 
• DVC operates a network of major dams including **Tilaiya**, **Konar**, **Maithon**, and **Panchet**, which regulate the flow of the **Damodar River** and its tributaries like the **Barakar River**.
 
• The corporation is a major producer of **electricity**, utilizing both **hydro-electric** and **thermal power** stations to fuel the industrial growth of the **Chhota Nagpur plateau**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Steel Production**:

 
 
• While the DVC area encompasses the **Steel Hub of India** (including **Bokaro** and **Durgapur**), the corporation itself provides the **power and water infrastructure** rather than engaging in the manufacturing process of steel.
 
 
 
• **Trade Promotion**:
 
 
• This refers to activities intended to stimulate the **exchange of goods**. Although DVC supports the economy, it is a **resource management** agency and not a trade-facilitating body.
 
 
 
• **Rural Credit**:
 
 
• This involves providing **financial loans** to the agricultural sector, which is the specialized function of institutions like **NABARD** and **Regional Rural Banks**, not a river valley corporation.
 
 
 
• **Socio-Economic Impact**:
 
 
• Beyond its engineering goals, DVC is responsible for **afforestation**, **malaria control**, and the **socio-economic well-being** of the inhabitants living within the **Damodar Valley**.

questions.question: The Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-Dhan (PM-SYM) scheme is designed for which group?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Unorganized Sector Workers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-Dhan (PM-SYM)** is a **Central Sector Scheme** launched by the **Ministry of Labour and Employment** in **February 2019** to provide old-age protection and social security.
 
• The scheme is specifically designed for **Unorganized Sector Workers**, a demographic that constitutes nearly **93 percent** of India total workforce and often lacks formal pension support.
 
• To be eligible, an applicant must fall within the **entry age of 18 to 40 years**, ensuring a consistent contribution period before reaching retirement.
 
• The scheme targets low-wage earners with a **monthly income of 15,000 rupees or less**, focusing on those most vulnerable to economic instability in their later years.
 
• Under this initiative, subscribers receive a **minimum assured monthly pension of 3,000 rupees** once they attain the age of **60 years**.
 
• The financial structure is based on a **50:50 matching contribution**, where the **Central Government** contributes an amount equal to the monthly premium paid by the beneficiary.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Targeted Occupational Groups**:

 
 
• Beneficiaries include **street vendors**, **mid-day meal workers**, **head loaders**, **brick kiln workers**, **cobblers**, **rag pickers**, **domestic workers**, and **agricultural laborers**.
 
• It also encompasses **handloom workers**, **leather workers**, and those engaged in similar informal occupations.
 
 
 
• **Exclusion Criteria**:
 
 
• Workers already covered under organized social security frameworks like the **Employees’ Provident Fund Organization (EPFO)**, **Employee State Insurance Corporation (ESIC)**, or the **National Pension System (NPS)** are ineligible.
 
• Individuals who fall under the **income taxpayer** bracket are also excluded from the benefits of the PM-SYM scheme.
 
 
 
• **Administrative Framework**:
 
 
• The **Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC)** serves as the **Pension Fund Manager** and is responsible for the disbursement of the monthly pension.
 
• Enrollment is conducted through **Common Service Centres (CSCs)** using an **Aadhar card** and a **Savings Bank Account** or **Jan Dhan account** with **IFSC**.
 
• In the event of the subscriber death, the **spouse** is entitled to receive **50 percent** of the pension as a family pension, provided the spouse is not already a beneficiary.

questions.question: Which institution is entrusted with the formulation and implementation of India's foreign trade policy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT)** is an attached office of the **Ministry of Commerce and Industry** and is headed by the **Director General of Foreign Trade**.
 
• It is the apex body entrusted with the **formulation and implementation** of the **Foreign Trade Policy (FTP)** of India, which serves as the primary legal framework for the country's international trade.
 
• The organization transitioned from a **regulatory** regime to a **facilitatory** one following the **economic liberalization** of **1991**, evolving from the former office of the **Chief Controller of Imports and Exports (CCI&E)**.
 
• DGFT is responsible for issuing the **Importer-Exporter Code (IEC)**, a 10-digit identification number that is mandatory for any person or entity to engage in **import-export business** within the Indian territory.
 
• The institution manages various export incentive schemes, ensures compliance with **international trade obligations**, and provides a platform for resolving trade-related grievances through its network of **Regional Authorities (RAs)** across the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Foreign Trade Policy (FTP) 2023**:

 
 
• Transitioned from an **incentive-based** to a **remission-based** regime to ensure compatibility with **World Trade Organization (WTO)** norms.
 
• Focuses on the **Ease of Doing Business** through **paperless** and **automated** approval systems managed by DGFT.
 
 
 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**:
 
 
• Functions as India's **Central Bank**, managing **monetary policy** and the **Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), 1999**, rather than trade policy formulation.
 
 
 
• **NITI Aayog**:
 
 
• A **policy think tank** of the Government of India that provides directional and policy inputs; it does not have the executive mandate to implement **trade regulations**.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Home Affairs**:
 
 
• Responsible for **internal security**, **border management**, and **center-state relations**, having no direct role in the commercial aspects of **foreign trade**.

questions.question: According to the new policy for central government-run schools, what support is offered to students who fail their annual exams in Classes 5 and 8?

options.text: Additional coaching and a re-exam opportunity
Direct promotion to the next class

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Additional coaching and a re-exam opportunity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The policy for central government-run schools, including **Kendriya Vidyalayas (KVS)** and **Navodaya Vidyalayas (NVS)**, is governed by the **Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (Amendment) Act, 2019**, which modified the previous **No-Detention Policy**.
 
• Under the revised guidelines, students in **Class 5** and **Class 8** are required to appear for **regular annual examinations** at the end of each academic year to assess their learning progress.
 
• If a student fails to secure the minimum passing marks in these annual exams, the school is legally obligated to provide **additional instructions** or **remedial coaching** specifically targeted at the subjects the student failed.
 
• Following the period of **additional coaching**, the student must be granted a **re-examination opportunity** within a period of **two months** from the date of the original result declaration.
 
• The primary objective of this provision is to ensure that the student is not immediately detained and is given a fair chance to bridge **learning gaps** and demonstrate proficiency before a final decision on detention is made.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **RTE Act 2009 vs. 2019 Amendment**:

 
 
• The original **RTE Act of 2009** mandated that no child shall be held back in any class until the completion of elementary education (up to Class 8).
 
• The **2019 Amendment** was introduced to address concerns regarding falling **educational standards** and the lack of accountability in the learning process.
 
• It gives the **appropriate government** (Central or State) the power to decide whether to continue the no-detention policy or allow schools to detain students who fail the re-examination.
 
• The **National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT)** provides the framework for these assessments to ensure they align with defined **Learning Outcomes** for each grade level.

questions.question: In India, in which of the following year, the Space commission was established?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1972**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Space Commission** was established by the **Government of India** in **June 1972** to promote the rapid development and application of **space technology** for the nation's socio-economic benefits.
 
• Simultaneously, the **Department of Space (DOS)** was created to execute the policies formulated by the commission and provide administrative support to the space program.
 
• In **September 1972**, the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**, which was previously part of the Department of Atomic Energy, was brought under the administrative control of the **Department of Space**.
 
• The **Space Commission** serves as the highest policy-making body for space activities in India, overseeing the implementation of major projects like **satellite communications** and **planetary exploration**.
 
• This organizational structure ensures that the **Indian Space Program** remains directly under the purview of the **Prime Minister of India**, allowing for strategic decision-making and functional autonomy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Evolution of Space Research in India**:

 
 
• **1962**: The **Indian National Committee for Space Research (INCOSPAR)** was set up by the **Department of Atomic Energy** under the leadership of **Dr. Vikram Sarabhai**.
 
• **1969**: **ISRO** was established on **August 15**, replacing INCOSPAR to better organize space activities under a dedicated research organization.
 
• **Dr. Vikram Sarabhai** is globally recognized as the **Father of the Indian Space Program** for his vision in initiating India's space odyssey.
 
• The **Chairman of ISRO** concurrently serves as the **Chairman of the Space Commission** and the **Secretary of the Department of Space**, ensuring streamlined management.
 
• The **Department of Space** is headquartered in **Bengaluru**, Karnataka, which functions as the primary nerve center for all major Indian space missions.

questions.question: As per Annual Report, Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), 2023-24, the literacy rate among Muslims was ____ for persons aged 7 years & above.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**79.5%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)** for the period **July 2023 to June 2024** provides comprehensive data on education and employment across different religious groups in India.
 
• According to the **Annual Report 2023-24**, the literacy rate among the **Muslim** population for persons aged **7 years and above** is recorded at **79.5%**.
 
• A person is considered literate if they can both read and write with understanding in any language. The survey excludes children aged below **7 years** from this calculation.
 
• The data indicates a progressive increase in the literacy levels of the community when compared to previous rounds, such as the **2022-23** survey where the rate was approximately **77.7%**.
 
• The survey findings are pivotal for the **Ministry of Minority Affairs** and other government bodies to design targeted educational interventions and welfare schemes for minority communities.
 
• The literacy rate is further bifurcated into **Rural** and **Urban** sectors, where urban areas typically exhibit a higher percentage of literate individuals compared to rural regions due to better access to educational infrastructure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)**:

 
 
• It was launched by the **National Sample Survey Office (NSSO)** in **April 2017** to provide more frequent and reliable labor market statistics.
 
• The survey operates under the aegis of the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)**.
 
• It uses two primary metrics for employment data: **Usual Status (ps+ss)** and **Current Weekly Status (CWS)**.
 
 
 
• **Key Survey Indicators**:
 
 
• **Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR)**: The percentage of the population that is either working or actively seeking work.
 
• **Worker Population Ratio (WPR)**: The percentage of employed persons within the total population.
 
• **Unemployment Rate (UR)**: The percentage of persons unemployed among those in the labour force.
 
 
 
• **Data Collection Methodology**:
 
 
• The **PLFS** employs a **Rotational Panel Sampling** design in urban areas to capture short-term changes in the labor market every quarter.
 
• For rural areas, the samples are drawn annually to provide a broad overview of the agrarian and non-farm employment landscape.

questions.question: In Southern Asia region, which country topped in the Global Gender Gap Index 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bangladesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Global Gender Gap Index** is an annual benchmark published by the **World Economic Forum (WEF)** that assesses gender parity across four critical dimensions: **Economic Participation and Opportunity**, **Educational Attainment**, **Health and Survival**, and **Political Empowerment**.
 
• In the **Southern Asia** region, **Bangladesh** has consistently maintained its position as the top-ranked country, a trend reflected in the **2025** data where it leads its neighbors in closing the overall gender gap.
 
• A primary driver for the high ranking of **Bangladesh** is its significant score in the **Political Empowerment** sub-index, owing to the long-standing presence of women in **Head of State** positions and high representation in the **National Parliament**.
 
• The country has achieved near-parity in **primary and secondary education** enrollment, which has been a cornerstone of its social development strategy over the past few decades.
 
• While the **Southern Asia** region as a whole faces challenges in **Economic Participation**, **Bangladesh** has demonstrated relatively better integration of women into the **labor force** compared to regional averages.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Global Gender Gap Index Framework**:

 
 
• The index provides scores ranging from **0 to 1**, where **1.0** signifies full gender parity and **0** signifies complete imparity.
 
• It serves as a tool for **policymakers** to track progress and identify specific areas requiring **legislative** or **socio-economic** interventions.
 
 
 
• **Regional Comparison**:
 
 
• **Nepal** and **Bhutan** often rank closely behind **Bangladesh**, showing notable improvements in **Health and Survival** and **literacy rates**.
 
• **Maldives** performs well in **Educational Attainment** but faces gaps in **Political Empowerment** relative to the top performers in the region.
 
• The **Southern Asia** region generally requires focused efforts on **Economic Participation** to reach global parity levels seen in regions like **Europe** or **North America**.
